ground_truth.description: _claimFees() sweeps the entire balance of `token0`/`token1` after `collectFees()`, stealing rewards if `rewardToken` matches `token0` or `token1`. Impact: Bribe contract receives staking rewards instead of fees.
ground_truth.root_cause: _claimFees() sweeps the entire balance of `token0`/`token1` after `collectFees()`, stealing rewards if `rewardToken` matches `token0` or `token1`. Impact: Bribe contract receives staking rewards instead of fees.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: A test deposits 10 HYBR rewards, adds 0.1 HYBR fees, and `claimFees()` sweeps all 10.1 HYBR to the bribe contract.
ground_truth.fix_description: Transfer only the difference in balance before/after `collectFees()`; add access control to `claimFees`. Status: Mitigation confirmed.

vulnerabilities.explanation: The _claimFees function transfers the entire balance of token0 and token1 from the contract after calling collectFees(), rather than transferring only the newly collected fees. This means if the rewardToken matches either token0 or token1, staking rewards deposited into the gauge will also be swept and sent to the bribe contract as fees.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. An attacker deposits staking rewards (if rewardToken equals token0 or token1) into the gauge 2. User calls claimFees() which calls _claimFees() 3. collectFees() is called, adding actual LP fees to the contract 4. The function calculates claimed0/claimed1 as the entire balance (including both fees and staking rewards) 5. All tokens (fees + staking rewards) are sent to the internal bribe contract as 'fees'
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Track token balances before calling collectFees() and only transfer the difference in balances as actual fees. Add access control to restrict who can call claimFees() if needed.

prediction.overall_explanation: The contract has a critical logic error in the _claimFees function where it transfers the entire token balance instead of only the newly collected fees. This allows staking rewards to be stolen when they share the same address as one of the pool tokens, causing them to be mistakenly treated as LP fees and sent to the bribe contract.
